clue.text: People taking lessons in Cheltenham, for example

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
a course is a series of lessons

explanation.surface: Pupils attending classes in the Gloucestershire spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham reads as a school town, but here it is the racing venue in Gloucestershire, home of the Cheltenham Festival of horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheltenham is a famous English venue where horses run, an example of a track for racing.

clue.text: Shake firm support

definitions.meaning: to shake something is to make it sway to and fro
a dependable person or foundation, someone you can lean on

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to sway violently and a steady, reliable support.

clue.text: Rabbit with fluffy tail

parts.note: con is the Italian and Spanish word for with

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, here of fluffy

explanation.surface: A bunny with a fluffy tail.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for the rabbit, still used for its fur.

clue.text: Conventionally pretty and sweet container

definitions.meaning: describing scenery that is attractive in a clichéd, twee way
a box holding confectionery made from cocoa

explanation.definitionFit: Twee scenes like those printed on lids of confectionery packaging gave the phrase its sense of clichéd prettiness.

clue.text: Discourage a peace-keeper?

definitions.meaning: to deprive of courage or nerve
a United Nations soldier, read as UN plus man

explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone of nerve; split up, it is also a member of a United Nations force.

clue.text: Tree, as far as possible, put on board

indicators.note: something put on board a ship sits inside its letters, so this signals a container

parts.note: on board means aboard a ship, SS being a steamship

indicators.note: possible suggests the letters can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A tree that is loaded aboard as far as can be managed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' looks like part of the phrase 'as far as possible', but it is the anagram signal; 'on board' conventionally means inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American laurel whose bark and roots were used for flavouring.

clue.text: Wife married to that fellow? Fancy that!

parts.note: him refers to a male person already mentioned

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a wife has wed a particular man.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a sudden notion or caprice.

clue.text: Unable to get out of York, say, before spring

parts.note: York is an English royal house, the House of York
to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in York until the spring arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: York looks like the city, but it is the royal dynasty, as in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Confined to one's home, typically by illness or age.

clue.text: Mark deadliest disturbance in this troubled region

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Signs of the most lethal unrest in a war-torn part of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of southwest Asia and North Africa, long the scene of conflict.

clue.text: Sticking to the rules, prisoner with criminal record is given time …

parts.note: a con is a convict
form is British slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: A rule-abiding prisoner with previous convictions is sentenced.
explanation.walkthrough: FORM is British slang for a record of past convictions. The clue runs on into the next one through the ellipsis.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who complies with accepted standards and behaves as expected.

clue.text: … in prison, as court pronounced

indicators.note: pronounced says the word for the court is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a court enclosed by buildings

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: a convict jailed, as the court declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' wants to be a law court; it is a college quadrangle. The leading 'in' belongs to the previous clue's sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Quod is old British slang for a jail.

clue.text: Eats a rare cut, cooked in addition to fish

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients prepared and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eats a joint of meat served rare.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayonnaise-based condiment served alongside battered or breaded seafood.

clue.text: Fit enough to go like the clappers?

definitions.text: Fit enough to go like the clappers?

parts.words: Fit enough to go like the clappers?
parts.note: a fit, healthy person is said to be in perfect condition, like a bell ringing clearly; clappers are what make a bell ring

explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning in perfect health, from a bell ringing true.

clue.text: Those suffering from it are highly disturbed

definitions.text: Those suffering from it are highly disturbed

parts.words: Those suffering from it are highly disturbed
parts.note: highly disturbed seems to mean very upset, but read as disturbed by being high up it describes a fear of heights

explanation.definitionFit: A morbid fear of high places.

clue.text: Asian has to subscribe for spell in US

parts.note: an Indian is an Asian from India
to subscribe is to sign one's name to a document

explanation.surface: An Asian person must pay up for a stint in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like a period of time; it is an enchantment, a US idiom for a hold over someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An American expression for a hex or controlling influence over another person.

clue.text: Sails south with hesitation -one checks how wind is blowing

definitions.text: one checks how wind is blowing

parts.note: a ship's sails are its canvas
er is the sound of a hesitation

explanation.surface: A sailor setting sails southward, hesitating, tests the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: The wind is not weather but public opinion: an election worker gauges how voters are leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A person soliciting votes door to door finds out which way opinion leans.

clue.text: Because bank appears to be in good faith

parts.note: since means because
to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A bank seems trustworthy for some reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Done honestly and genuinely, as in signing off a letter.

clue.text: Start off barbecue in style — grill meat on this?

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the word for style

parts.note: tone is style or manner

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of barbecue

explanation.surface: Launching a barbecue with flair by grilling a steak.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the meat is cooked on the bone of that shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak cut containing a bone shaped like a letter, so the meat cooks around it.

clue.text: Nothing pleasant held in reserve

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Nothing agreeable is being kept back.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in the freezer, figuratively, is to postpone or keep it aside.

clue.text: Without limitations, as a brass band has?

definitions.meaning: a brass band has wind and percussion instruments, none with strings

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an arrangement free of conditions, and literally a band lacking stringed instruments.

clue.text: Making rapid progress, deliver Duke

parts.note: to hand over is to deliver
dukes is slang for fists

explanation.surface: A nobleman is delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke looks like the nobleman; it is old slang for a fist, as in 'put up your dukes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually of money, gaining it quickly and in large amounts.

clue.text: Give up supporting game out East

parts.note: for means in favour of
go is a board game from East Asia

explanation.surface: Abandoning support for a game played in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to relinquish or do without it.

clue.text: Quickly read second novel

parts.note: Kim is a novel by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: Speed-reading a second novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim is to glance through a text quickly.

clue.text: Pot, say, a small reptile

indicators.note: say signals that a word is spoken aloud to give a similar-sounding one

parts.note: a crock is an earthenware pot

explanation.surface: A pot, for instance, and a little lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' signals a shortened word: the clipped form of crocodile.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipped, informal form of crocodile, the shortened name being the small part.

clue.text: See red and black painting

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: Viewing a painting done in red and black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See red' looks like a viewing instruction; it is the idiom for becoming angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe with anger, as when one's blood is said to be seething.

clue.text: Material fool put on prophet

indicators.note: in an across clue, the fool put on the prophet comes after it

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
a sucker is a fool, someone easily duped

explanation.surface: A fool is placed above a prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: A light puckered cotton fabric, often striped.

clue.text: Composer of incidental music in earnest

indicators.note: in shows the answer is contained within the following word

explanation.surface: A composer who wrote background music seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne, the 18th-century English composer, wrote much incidental music for the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne wrote theatre scores including the song Rule, Britannia!

clue.text: Initially harmed by dreadful medic with ropy syringe

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word harmed
dreadful suggests something botched, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient harmed by a terrible doctor wielding a dodgy syringe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'dreadful' with the medic, but it is the anagram signal, working only on the words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow needle and plunger for injecting under the skin.
